title: Returning Member Miles on Summit Retro Credits
content:
The Crestline Summit Loyalty Program gives returning-member miles on a retro credit according to how soon after the membership's latest inactivity forfeiture the credited segment was flown.

**Rule.** Count the calendar days from the date of the latest inactivity forfeiture entry on the membership to the flight date of the credited segment.

- A segment flown 0 to 90 days after that forfeiture adds 25 percent of the credit's base miles, rounded up to the next hundred miles.
- A segment flown more than 90 and up to 365 days after it adds a flat 1000 miles, whatever the base miles.
- A segment flown before any inactivity forfeiture, more than 365 days after one, or on a membership with no inactivity forfeiture adds no returning-member miles.

The base miles are the eligible fare multiplied by the award miles per dollar of the tier the member holds on the day the credit posts, rounded to the nearest whole mile with halves rounded up. Only forfeitures made on the ground of inactivity count; a forfeiture on account closure does not. The addition is computed on the base miles and added to the miles the credit carries.

### Training questions

**Which forfeiture is used when there are several?** The latest inactivity forfeiture entry on the membership.

**What if the segment was flown on the forfeiture date itself?** That is day 0, inside the first span.

**Boundary days (hypothetical forfeiture dated 1 February 2025):**

| Flight date | Days after the forfeiture | Addition |
|---|---|---|
| 31 January 2025 | before it | None |
| 1 February 2025 | 0 | 25 percent of base miles, rounded up to the hundred |
| 2 May 2025 | 90 | 25 percent of base miles, rounded up to the hundred |
| 3 May 2025 | 91 | 1000 miles |
| 1 February 2026 | 365 | 1000 miles |
| 2 February 2026 | 366 | None |

**How is the hundred rounding done?** Upwards to the next whole hundred (hypothetical base miles): 25 percent of 2231 is 557.75, which becomes 600; 25 percent of 2400 is exactly 600 and stays 600.
